artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Hand. Cannot. Erase." is the fourth solo studio album by English musician Steven Wilson, released in 2015 on the Kscope label. The album is a progressive rock work that blends intricate musicianship with a conceptual narrative. It tells the story of a young woman living in a city who mysteriously disappears without anyone noticing for years, exploring themes of isolation and anonymity in modern urban life. Musically, it features a rich, layered sound with contributions from notable musicians such as Guthrie Govan (guitar), Adam Holzman (keyboards), Theo Travis (flute/saxophone), Nick Beggs (bass/stick), and Marco Minnemann (drums), recorded at London's AIR Studios.

Positioned as a significant entry in Wilson's discography, "Hand. Cannot. Erase." follows his earlier solo works and showcases his evolution towards more narrative-driven and emotionally complex compositions. The album received critical acclaim for its ambitious concept, sophisticated arrangements, and production quality, further cementing Wilson's reputation as a leading figure in contemporary progressive rock. It was also commercially successful within its genre, supported by a UK and European tour following its release. The album's original release in early 2015 was later commemorated with a 10th anniversary edition featuring remastered audio and special vinyl packaging.
